newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 4.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:

* The United States, Britain and France have agreed to freeze the distribution of $68 million in gold bars that were looted by the Nazis from European central banks, and Clinton Administration officials say the gold could be used to form a fund for Holocaust survivors.

* The Pakistan Muslim League party of Nawaz Sharif was positioned to win at least 100 seats in Pakistan's 217-seat National Assembly in early election results, indicating a sharp defeat for former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.

* The Army's highest-ranking enlisted man, a sergeant major who also serves on an Army sexual harassment panel, asked to be excused from his panel duties after a 22-year Army veteran accused him of sexually assaulting her.
* Many of the roughly 1,800 chimpanzees in captivity for use in American biomedical research are unneeded, stirring debate over the futures of these surplus chimps.
* A special prosecutor's investigation has found that New York State troopers were able to plant evidence in criminal cases, including some of the state's most infamous criminal cases.
* At least 1,000 New York City public school students are expected to enter private schools on a plan supported by Mayor Rudolph Giuliani.
